items.title: fix(desktop): make Cline and Cline Pass sign-out stick
items.body:
### Related Issue

User reports that signing out of the Cline account (Cline usage / Cline Pass) in the desktop app does not stick.

### Description

The desktop app has two ways to sign out of Cline, and two separate bugs kept users signed in:

1. **Providers page > Cline > Sign out** sends `enabled: false`, which deletes the `cline` entry from `providers.json`. `ProviderSettingsManager` re-runs the legacy import on every construction (i.e. every sidecar command) and re-adds `cline` from the classic VS Code extension's `~/.cline/data/secrets.json` (`cline:clineAccountId` / `clineApiKey`). This is the same root cause as the ChatGPT/Codex sign-out fix in #14040, which only cleared the Codex secret.

2. **Providers page > Cline Pass > Sign out** did nothing at all. `cline-pass` is registered with `storageProviderId: "cline"`, so its credentials live under the `cline` entry; deleting only the `cline-pass` entry left the account signed in.

(The Account page > Sign out path blanks the auth block but keeps the entry, so it was never affected.)

Changes, all in `apps/examples/desktop-app/sidecar`:

- `legacy-codex-credentials.ts` -> `legacy-provider-credentials.ts`: `clearLegacyCodexCredentials()` becomes `clearLegacyProviderCredentials(providerId)` driven by a small provider-to-secret-keys map (`openai-codex`, `cline`). Same semantics otherwise: missing/unparseable file is a no-op, failed write throws so the webview reports the sign-out as failed.
- `commands.ts` `save_provider_settings`: when a provider is disabled, also disable its `storageProviderId` if different (Cline Pass -> Cline), then clear that provider's legacy secrets.

### Test Procedure

- Extended `legacy-provider-credentials.test.ts` to cover the `cline` keys and an unknown provider id.
- `bun run test:sidecar` (26 files, 306 tests) passes; `tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json --noEmit` and `biome check` are clean on the changed files.
- End-to-end check through the real `handleCommand` with `CLINE_DATA_DIR` pointed at a temp dir seeded with a legacy `secrets.json`:

```
0) fresh open (legacy import): providers= [ "cline", "openrouter" ] clineToken= legacy-id-token clinePassToken= legacy-id-token
1) after Cline sign-out, next command: providers= [ "openrouter", "cline" ] clineToken= undefined clinePassToken= undefined
   secrets.json now: { "openRouterApiKey": "sk-or-keep" }
2) signed in with cline + cline-pass: providers= [ "openrouter", "cline", "cline-pass" ] clineToken= fresh clinePassToken= fresh
3) after Cline Pass sign-out, next command: providers= [ "openrouter", "cline" ] clineToken= undefined clinePassToken= undefined
```

Before this change, step 1 came back with `clineToken= legacy-id-token` and step 3 with `clinePassToken= fresh`.

### Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

### Pre-flight Checklist

-   [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs)
-   [x] Tests are passing (`bun test`) and code is formatted and linted (`bun run format && bun run lint`)
-   [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Additional Notes

The underlying issue remains that the legacy import runs on every `ProviderSettingsManager` construction; an import-once approach was tried and reverted inside #14040, so per-provider secret clearing is the pragmatic patch until the legacy import is retired.
